newsitem.title: IRAN: Iranian artists to celebrate Khatami victory.
newsitem.headline: Iranian artists to celebrate Khatami victory.

text.p: A group of Iranian artists said they planned plan to distribute sweets on Monday at Tehran cinemas to celebrate Mohammad Khatami's rise to power as new president of the Islamic republic.
Khatami, 54, is to take the oath of office in parliament on Monday after his crushing victory over a conservative candidate in May elections.

In 1992 Khatami, a Moslem Shi'ite clergyman seen as a moderate, was forced to resign as culture minister by conservatives who accused him of failing to stamp out what they saw as a Western cultural invasion and of allowing films, plays and books which clashed with the country's Islamic beliefs.

Satellite dishes, an important window on the outside world, were banned and confiscated. Diplomats said that in pre-election television debates Khatami turned down invitations to back the move but neither did he commit himself to allowing dishes again if he won.
Many artists, young people and women expect the new president to relax some social constraints.

Some young people hope he will allow the import of music by popular Iranian singers living in exile, mainly in the United States and Europe, and ease restrictions on Western music. Tehran has a flourishing black market in music.
